title: Scripture holds the substance — not every rite left to church prudence
source_text: VII. Res prioris generis asserimus sacra Scriptura contineri, non item alias istas, quae sunt ad Ecclesiae fidem, mores & disciplinam veluti accidentariae. Multa enim quae pertinent ad varias divini cultus & Ecclesiasticae politiae circumstantias, fatemur non esse sigillatim in Scriptura tradita, sed relicta prudentiae praepositorum Ecclesiae, sub hoc generali praecepto, ut omnia fiant ordine & decenter in Ecclesia Dei. Unde patet ab Ecclesiae Romanae Doctoribus frustra contra nos in hac controversia, varias instantias peti a ritibus, statutis & caeremoniis quibusdam, quae in Ecclesia antiqua, sive judaica sive Christiana, olim observata sunt, & etiamnum apud nos servantur tam in divino cultu, quam in politia Ecclesiastica, etiamsi nihil de iis in Scriptura constitutum sit.
pass_a_gloss: Things of the former kind we assert are contained by sacred Scripture; not likewise those other things which are as it were accidental to the faith, morals, and discipline of the Church. For many things which pertain to various circumstances of divine worship and of ecclesiastical polity we confess are not handed down piece by piece in Scripture, but left to the prudence of the overseers of the Church, under this general precept, that all things be done in order and decently in the Church of God. Whence it is plain that by the Doctors of the Roman Church various instances are sought in vain against us in this controversy from certain rites, statutes, and ceremonies which were once observed in the ancient Church, whether Jewish or Christian, and are still kept among us both in divine worship and in ecclesiastical polity, even if nothing about them is established in Scripture.
pass_b_english: We say Scripture contains the former kind — the substance — not those accidental appendages of church faith, morals, and discipline.

Many circumstances of worship and church polity are not set out item by item in Scripture; they are left to the prudence of church overseers under the general rule that all things be done decently and in order in God’s Church.

So Rome’s doctors waste their shot when they press old Jewish or Christian rites, statutes, and ceremonies — still kept among us in worship and polity — as if their absence from a Scripture catalogue refuted us.

lemmas.gloss: piece by piece / one by one

choices.why: Not every circumstance spelled out singly in Scripture.
